rationale: A pluggable exporter class implementing the Exporter interface. It converts the model into GraphML for external visualization tools. It is a replaceable unit used by the export command and the MCP export manager, which makes it an application component of notable but not central significance. It starts its own telemetry span, so observability is flagged.

A private string-sanitizing helper that replaces path traversal and illegal filename characters. It is a trivial formatting utility used by the save methods and is an implementation detail, not an architectural element. It performs no I/O itself.

A small exported helper in the relationship CLI command module that looks up the cardinality and strength of a relationship from the catalog. It is an internal lookup with minor architectural weight and implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

A passive in-code TypeScript interface that carries changeset diff state (additions, modifications, deletions) between the virtual projection and diff/preview display. It is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is notable within the changeset projection module.

A bundled JSON schema document that defines the node schemas for the testing layer's 17 element types, each with $schema, $id and attribute constraints. It is a core data-model contract the tool validates models against, not a test asset itself, so it is modelled as a data-model JSONSchema document of high architectural significance.

Nested recursive helper inside computeDirectoryHashes that walks a directory and hashes files. It is a private implementation detail below model granularity; it reads files from disk (data persistence) and logs errors only incidentally via console.error.

CopilotClient is a concrete adapter component, extending BaseChatClient, that integrates with the external GitHub Copilot CLI by spawning subprocesses and streaming responses. It is an integration point, so it is modelled as an application component. It also emits telemetry spans and logs chat messages itself.

A readonly TypeScript interface that holds backup manifest state (the list of files and a timestamp). It has no behaviour of its own and is not published as a schema, so it is an application data object. As a minor type in a shared types file with no callers, it rates low significance and does not itself perform persistence.

Internal helper method of CbmAnalyzer that normalizes a raw CBM graph node into a route record with defaults. It is a data-shaping helper called only by verify(), and an implementation detail rather than a named architectural element.

GapAnalyzer is a cohesive class within the audit subsystem. It detects missing relationships per layer using templates and is composed by AuditOrchestrator. It is a notable internal unit of the relationship-audit module rather than a system boundary, and it has no I/O, auth or UI concerns of its own.

Static configuration module defining per-layer relationship templates (LayerTemplate interface plus LAYER_TEMPLATES constant) used by the audit gap-analysis feature. It is passive reference data rather than behaviour, so it is modelled as an application data object. A maintainer would name it when explaining the relationship audit, but it is not a central element.

Plain exported TypeScript interface carrying validation status fields as part of a stats collector result. It is a passive in-code data structure, neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject of minor significance.

Utility module providing SHA256 file hashing for change detection of integration files. It is a generic helper below the granularity of an architectural element, though it reads files from disk. A minor internal unit supporting the integration installer's change detection.

A trivial terminal-colour formatting getter that wraps ansis bold green behind a colour-support check. It is a formatting utility below architectural granularity, so it is not a model element. It styles strings but does not itself render or drive the UI.

BFS traversal over the in-memory GraphModel, exposed via Model.traverse. It is a notable internal graph-query behaviour of the core model component, best modelled as an application function rather than an element in its own right. It performs no I/O and touches no cross-cutting concern.

Core class that loads predicate and relationship-schema definitions from bundled JSON files and exposes the relationship catalog. Audit orchestrators, CLI commands and the report model all use it, so it is a central application component. It reads durable schema files from disk.

A small internal type describing the base shape of compiled spec data (specVersion, schemas, predicates) used inside the spec loader. It is a structural helper type with no callers, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.
